home.s003: Do I really need Form 5472 and Form 1120 if my LLC made no money?
home.s004: Likely yes. Form 5472 reports reportable transactions, which includes any capital you put in or distributions you took out — not just revenue. The pro forma Form 1120 is always required as the attachment vehicle whenever Form 5472 is required, even with zero income.
home.s006: Yes — every plan includes fax delivery to the IRS Ogden PIN Unit and a timestamped provider transmission receipt. Keep it with your submitted package; it is transmission evidence, not IRS acceptance or a guarantee of penalty relief. You don't need your own fax machine.
home.s007: Why does the IRS require fax instead of e-file?
home.s008: Foreign-owned U.S. disregarded entities cannot use ordinary corporate e-file for this Form 5472 and pro forma Form 1120 package. The special IRS instructions allow fax to +1-855-887-7737 or mail to the dedicated Ogden PIN Unit address. Our service uses fax and supplies the provider transmission receipt.
home.s010: No. The price you see is the price you pay. No setup fee, no monthly subscription, no per-page fax surcharge. Multi-year filings add a flat {value1} per additional past year — disclosed up front and shown in the checkout summary before you pay.
home.s011: Do you store my bank statements or signed forms?
home.s012: Yes, with your filing. The bank statement files you upload and the transactions taken from them are stored so we can prepare and review your return. Your signed forms, the exact PDF we fax to the IRS and the fax receipt are kept in your account for up to 7 years so you can download them. Ask us and we delete them sooner.
home.s014: 100% money-back guarantee if we fail to submit your filing to the IRS. If the fax doesn't deliver on the first send, we automatically retry. If it still fails, you get a full refund — no questions asked. And if the IRS ever assesses a penalty because of an error in our preparation, we handle the response with the IRS at no charge.

what-is-form-5472-who-files.q: What is Form 5472, and who has to file it?
what-is-form-5472-who-files.a: Form 5472 is the information return that reports related-party transactions. A foreign-owned US single-member LLC treated as a disregarded entity usually files Form 5472 with a pro forma Form 1120 when it has a reportable transaction during the tax year.

no-income-form-5472-form-1120.q: Do I really need Form 5472 and a Form 1120 if my LLC made no money?
no-income-form-5472-form-1120.a: Form 5472 and the pro forma Form 1120 are likely still needed even when your LLC made no money. No income is different from no reportable transactions, and formation costs, owner contributions, reimbursements, loans, or owner draws can create a filing requirement.

can-you-tell-me-whether-i-need-to-file.q: Can you tell me whether I need to file?
can-you-tell-me-whether-i-need-to-file.a: We can confirm whether your described situation fits our filing profile. If your US LLC is a single-member LLC owned by a non-US person and it had any reportable transaction during the year, including money moved in to open its bank account, it must file Form 5472 with a pro forma Form 1120.

what-is-pro-forma-form-1120.q: What is the pro forma Form 1120, and why is it attached?
what-is-pro-forma-form-1120.a: The pro forma Form 1120 is the cover document that lets Form 5472 be submitted as a valid IRS package. For foreign-owned single-member LLCs, Form 5472 is filed as an attachment to the pro forma Form 1120; neither form alone is valid for this filing.

what-counts-as-reportable-transaction.q: What counts as a reportable transaction?
what-counts-as-reportable-transaction.a: Reportable transactions are defined broadly and can include capital in, distributions out, any payment between you and the LLC, any loan, and any related-party transaction. Form 5472 reports those related-party transactions in dollar amounts, and Part V is where capital contributions, distributions, and most owner-to-LLC payments are reported.

capital-contributions-owner-reimbursemen.q: Do capital contributions and owner reimbursements count as reportable transactions?
capital-contributions-owner-reimbursemen.a: Capital contributions and owner reimbursements can count as reportable transactions. Capital contributions and distributions count, the seed money wired to open the bank account counts, and a reimbursement you took out for a business expense counts, even when the LLC had zero revenue.

can-form-5472-be-e-filed.q: Can Form 5472 be filed electronically, or only by fax or mail?
can-form-5472-be-e-filed.a: Only by fax or mail for a foreign-owned LLC. The IRS Form 5472 instructions say a foreign-owned U.S. disregarded entity cannot file Form 5472 electronically, so it goes with its pro forma Form 1120 by fax to +1-855-887-7737 or by mail to the IRS Ogden PIN Unit. Form5472 Prep prepares the package, faxes it there and sends you the transmission receipt.

first-year-llc-file.q: Does a first-year LLC still have to file?
first-year-llc-file.a: A first-year LLC still has to file if it had reportable transactions during its formation year. Review activity from formation onward, including formation costs paid by the owner. The year of formation counts, and the Form 5472 package follows the same deadline rules as other years.

dissolved-llc-still-file.q: My LLC was dissolved this year — do I still file?
dissolved-llc-still-file.a: A dissolved LLC still files Form 5472 for the partial year ending at dissolution. The deadline is generally the 15th day of the 4th month after the LLC’s final month; a short year ending in June of a tax year that began before 2026 is due the 15th day of the 3rd month instead.
dissolved-llc-still-file.learnMore: Final Form 5472 for a dissolved LLC

form-5472-deadline.a: The Form 5472 deadline for a calendar-year LLC is generally April 15, filed with the pro forma Form 1120. If Form 7004 is filed on time, the deadline can extend to October 15 because Form 5472 is attached to Form 1120. The extension process must be handled correctly.

form-7004-extension.q: How does the Form 7004 extension work?
form-7004-extension.a: Form 7004 must be filed by the original April 15 deadline. If Form 7004 is timely, it extends the Form 5472 package due date to October 15 because Form 5472 is attached to Form 1120. Without it, the April 15 deadline remains. We file it as a separate paid service: we fax it to the IRS Ogden PIN Unit and email the fax confirmation, which is not IRS acceptance.

no-income-no-transactions-deadline.q: Does having no income or no transactions change the deadline?
no-income-no-transactions-deadline.a: No income or no transactions does not change the Form 5472 deadline. The deadline itself does not change; Form 5472 is triggered by reportable transactions, not income, and if reportable transactions exist, the same due date applies even when the LLC had zero revenue.

missed-form-5472.q: What happens if Form 5472 is missed?
missed-form-5472.a: The IRS penalty is generally {amount1} for a missing or substantially incomplete Form 5472. If the IRS mails a notice and the failure continues for more than {days1} days after that notice, another {amount2} can be added for each {days2}-day period, or part of one, that it continues. Late filings can sometimes include a reasonable cause explanation under DIIRSP.

automatic-penalty.a: It can be. IRC §6038A(d) provides an initial {amount1} penalty when a reporting corporation fails to furnish required Form 5472 information on time or files a substantially incomplete return, and the IRS can assess it systemically when a late Form 5472 is processed, without a person reviewing the case first.

can-penalty-be-abated.a: The Form 5472 penalty can be abated, but there are no guarantees. Many late filers pursue reasonable-cause relief through DIIRSP by submitting the late return with a Reasonable Cause Statement. The IRS decides each case on its facts, and Treas. Reg. §1.6038A-4(b) requires showing reasonable cause and good faith.

cp15-notice.a: CP 215 is the IRS Notice of Penalty Charge for business accounts. The IRS manual (IRM 20.1.9.5.2) says a CP 215 is generated once a Form 5472 penalty is assessed; CP 15 is the equivalent notice for individual accounts. Check the amount, tax year and response date on it, and do not ignore it.

statute-of-limitations.q: Is there a statute of limitations?
statute-of-limitations.a: There is effectively no statute of limitations until a complete or substantially complete Form 5472 return is filed. Filing the return, even late, is what starts the clock; until then the year stays open indefinitely. That is why the missing package still matters.

missed-prior-years.q: What if I've missed prior years?
missed-prior-years.a: If you missed prior years, you can pick all the years you need to file when you start. We auto-flag the filing as DIIRSP and include a reasonable cause statement requesting penalty abatement, with additional past tax years priced at {amount1} each.

deadline-already-passed.q: The deadline already passed this year — what should I do now?
deadline-already-passed.a: If the Form 5472 deadline already passed, DIIRSP with a reasonable-cause statement is the standard remedy for a late Form 5472 package. If April 15 was missed without Form 7004, file the actual return under DIIRSP with the late filing package.

irs-notice-help.q: I've received an IRS penalty notice — can you still help?
irs-notice-help.a: Not with the penalty itself. We handle preventative late filings, made before the IRS sends a penalty notice. If you have already received a CP 215 notice or a §6038A penalty letter, contact a tax attorney or enrolled agent who handles international information return penalties. Separately, if an error in our own preparation ever causes a penalty, we handle the IRS response at no charge.

ein-needed-for-form-5472.q: Do I need an EIN to file Form 5472?
ein-needed-for-form-5472.a: Yes, Form 5472 requires your LLC’s EIN in the header. The EIN identifies the LLC as the reporting corporation on the package. We can handle both an EIN and a Form 5472 filing if you need both, so the identifier and filing package stay aligned.

what-is-an-ein.q: What is an EIN, and why does my LLC need one?
what-is-an-ein.a: An EIN is a 9-digit US tax ID issued by the IRS to business entities. Your LLC needs an EIN to open a US business bank account, set up Stripe or PayPal, hire US contractors, file Form 5472, and sign certain contracts.

apply-for-ein-myself.q: Can't I just apply for an EIN myself on the IRS website?
apply-for-ein-myself.a: The online EIN application on irs.gov is only available if you have a US Social Security Number or ITIN. Foreign nationals without a US tax ID cannot use the online tool, so the remaining route is Form SS-4 by fax or phone.

ssn-itin-needed-for-ein.q: Do I need a US Social Security Number or ITIN to get an EIN?
ssn-itin-needed-for-ein.a: No, a non-resident owner without an SSN or ITIN can obtain an EIN. Form SS-4 allows the responsible party’s tax ID to be marked “Foreign,” and the application goes to the IRS international unit. The online EIN tool is different and is only available if you already have a US SSN or ITIN.

ein-timing.q: How long does the EIN take?
ein-timing.a: An EIN typically takes {days1} business days once we have your documents. We call the IRS Business & Specialty Tax Line on your behalf and can often obtain the EIN on the call, while complex cases may take slightly longer.

already-have-ein.q: What if my LLC already has an EIN?
already-have-ein.a: If your LLC already has an EIN, you do not need the EIN service. Use that EIN for the LLC on the Form 5472 package. Form 5472 identifies the LLC as the reporting corporation and includes the LLC name, EIN, address, and total assets. We can also help retrieve a lost or forgotten EIN; contact support@form5472prep.com.

what-is-itin.q: What is an ITIN, and do I need one to run my US LLC?
what-is-itin.a: An ITIN is a 9-digit tax ID issued by the IRS to individuals who need to file or be identified on a US tax return but are not eligible for a Social Security Number. Many foreign-owned US LLC owners operate with just an EIN and never need an ITIN.

ein-vs-itin.q: What is the difference between an EIN and an ITIN?
ein-vs-itin.a: An EIN is assigned to a business entity, while an ITIN is assigned to an individual. Your LLC has an EIN; you as a person would have an ITIN or SSN. Most foreign-owned single-member LLC owners need an EIN but may or may not need an ITIN.

certifying-acceptance-agent.q: What is a Certifying Acceptance Agent, and how do you work with one?
certifying-acceptance-agent.a: A Certifying Acceptance Agent (CAA) can authenticate permitted identity documents for an ITIN application. We forward your application to an IRS-authorized CAA for the applicable document checks. A plain uploaded copy is not itself sufficient certification; follow the CAA's instructions. This route can avoid mailing an original passport to the IRS, but it does not guarantee ITIN eligibility or approval.

itin-timing.q: How long does the ITIN take?
itin-timing.a: The IRS says to allow {weeks1} weeks for an ITIN application status notice, or {weeks2} weeks when applying from overseas or during January 15 through April 30. These are processing estimates, not a guaranteed issuance date; requests for additional information can delay a decision.

itin-and-ein-same-time.q: Can I apply for an ITIN and an EIN at the same time?
itin-and-ein-same-time.a: Yes, contact us to coordinate separate EIN and ITIN applications when both are actually needed. The LLC's EIN and the individual's ITIN serve different purposes. Each application has its own eligibility, documentation and IRS processing timeline; obtaining one does not guarantee or automatically require the other.

process-start-to-finish.q: How does the process work, start to finish?
process-start-to-finish.a: You provide LLC and owner information, related-party transactions and year-end assets. We prepare the supported package for review, resolve signing requirements, and arrange IRS fax delivery. Keep the exact submitted package and provider transmission receipt together; the receipt documents transmission, not an IRS determination that the filing is complete or accepted.

fax-filing-included.q: Is fax filing to the IRS really included?
fax-filing-included.a: Yes, fax delivery to the IRS Ogden PIN Unit is included on every plan with no separate fee, so you do not need your own fax machine. The provider's timestamped receipt is transmission evidence, not an IRS-issued acceptance or a guarantee of penalty relief.

how-do-i-sign.q: How do I sign the forms?
how-do-i-sign.a: Once our tax accountant has reviewed your package, you read it and draw your signature once in your browser. We place your signature in the signature box of the pro forma Form 1120; Form 5472 itself has no taxpayer signature block. Only you sign your return — we never sign for you — and nothing in your Form 5472 package is sent to the IRS until you have signed.

how-long-whole-thing.q: How fast is Form5472 Prep Express filing?
how-long-whole-thing.a: Form5472 Prep Express filing ({amount1}) is ready for you to check and sign in under {days1} days from your order, {days2} days a week, and we fax it to the IRS once you sign. Standard filing ({amount2}) is ready in {days3} business days. Both tiers get the same package, accountant review and IRS fax delivery.

store-bank-statements-signed-forms.q: Do you store my bank statements or signed forms?
store-bank-statements-signed-forms.a: Yes, with your filing. The bank statement files you upload and the transactions taken from them are stored so we can prepare and review your return. Your signed forms, the exact PDF we fax to the IRS and the fax receipt are kept in your account for up to 7 years so you can download them. Ask us and we delete them sooner.

message-reply-time.q: How quickly will you reply to a message?
message-reply-time.a: We reply to messages within one business day, Monday to Friday, from support@form5472prep.com. The reply comes from that support address, so search for that sender if it is not in your inbox. Check your spam folder if you do not see the reply after you contact us.

accountants-formation-agents.q: Do you work with accountants and formation agents?
accountants-formation-agents.a: Yes, we work with formation agencies, registered agents, CPA and accounting firms, and consultants who manage US LLCs for multiple foreign-owned clients. Our partner program groups client filings under one partner account so one login shows live status for every client filing.

irs-received-filing-proof.q: How do I know the IRS received my filing?
irs-received-filing-proof.a: Inspect the provider receipt for the destination, timestamp, page count and reported transmission result. Keep it with the exact submitted package. That record is transmission evidence, not an IRS-issued acknowledgment of processing or acceptance. If delivery is uncertain or an IRS notice arrives, contact us and follow the notice's instructions and deadline.

irs-confirmation.q: Will the IRS send me a confirmation?
irs-confirmation.a: The current Form 5472 instructions do not describe a routine acceptance acknowledgment for this faxed package. A provider receipt and IRS processing are different things; silence proves neither acceptance nor rejection. Save your own submitted package and receipt rather than relying on indefinite portal storage, and do not resend solely because you have heard nothing.

next-year-reminder.q: Will you remind me next year?
next-year-reminder.a: Yes, we send a reminder in the second week of January for the next filing obligation, with a further reminder in March if it is still outstanding. The January reminder gives over three months’ notice, and for returning customers we pre-fill LLC and owner details from your most recent paid filing.

keep-records.q: How long should I keep my records?
keep-records.a: Keep the filed package, the IRS Fax Transmission Receipt, and our confirmation message with your LLC records for at least six years. If the filing was a final return for a dissolved LLC, keep the same documents with your permanent tax records for at least six years.

refund-policy.a: Fees are non-refundable once a PDF has been generated, except as expressly stated. Read that as the cutoff tied to the generated PDF for your filing package. Fees are refundable if we are unable to transmit your filing to the IRS after three attempts.

data-retention.q: How long do you keep my data?
data-retention.a: We retain fax transmission receipts for 7 years from the filing date, aggregated contribution and distribution totals for 7 years, entity and owner identification data for 7 years from last filing, payment records for 7 years, account email and login records for active use plus 12 months, and server access logs for {days1} days.

penalty.s001: Form 5472 Penalty Calculator — What Late Filing Costs
penalty.s002: Estimate Form 5472 late-filing exposure, see IRS penalty citations, and review the DIIRSP reasonable-cause path for catching up.
penalty.s003: Is the Form 5472 penalty really automatic?
penalty.s004: It can be. IRC §6038A(d) sets an initial {value1} penalty when a reporting corporation doesn't furnish the required Form 5472 information on time, and a substantially incomplete Form 5472 counts as not filed. The IRS manual says the penalty may be assessed systemically when a late Form 5472 is processed with a late Form 1120.
penalty.s006: Possibly, but there is no guarantee. Treas. Reg. §1.6038A-4(b) lets the IRS excuse a late Form 5472 for reasonable cause, decided case by case. First Time Abate generally does not apply to Form 5472 penalties.
penalty.s008: It is the IRS's Notice of Penalty Charge. The IRS manual says a CP 215 is generated and sent once a Form 5472 penalty is assessed. Once the IRS has notified you of the failure, continuation penalties can start {days1} days later if the filing is still not corrected.
penalty.s009: Does having no income exempt me from the penalty?
penalty.s010: No. A foreign-owned disregarded LLC can still have a Form 5472 and pro forma Form 1120 filing obligation even when it had no income, because reportable transactions can include contributions, distributions, and other owner-LLC activity.
penalty.s011: Is there a statute of limitations?
penalty.s012: Under IRC §6501(c)(8), the time to assess tax for a return or period the Form 5472 information relates to does not expire until 3 years after the IRS is furnished that information.
penalty.s013: Read the Form 5472 statute of limitations guide.
penalty.s017: The IRS can assess {amount1} per Form 5472, per year, often automatically when a late return is processed, and another {amount2} per {days1} days once {days2} days pass after a notice.
penalty.s018: Use this as a statutory exposure estimate, then compare it with the ordinary catch-up route: file the missing Form 5472 package and include a reasonable-cause statement under DIIRSP. How relief works is in our guide to the
penalty.s019: IRS penalty for late filing of Form 5472
penalty.s021: Estimate first, then fix the filing.
penalty.s022: The number below is not a prediction. It is a statutory framework calculator paired with the IRS's route for filing late information returns.
penalty.s025: The initial penalty is {value1} per Form 5472, per year. We use it as a statutory exposure estimate because the IRS can assess it when required Form 5472 information is late, missing, or substantially incomplete (often automatically when a late return is processed), before you compare the number with the ordinary catch-up route.
penalty.s027: After an IRS notice, there is a {value1}-day correction period. If the filing is still not fixed after that window, the statute adds {value2} for each {periodDays}-day period or part of one, so we treat the notice timeline separately from the initial per-form, per-year penalty estimate.
penalty.s029: Common triggers are never filing, filing Form 5472 without the required pro forma Form 1120, or sending an incomplete package. We also flag no-income cases, since a foreign-owned disregarded LLC can still have a filing obligation when reportable transactions include contributions, distributions, and other owner-LLC activity.
penalty.s031: If the IRS has not contacted you yet, the relief path is a DIIRSP filing that pairs late information returns with a reasonable-cause statement. We follow the ordinary catch-up route described above: file the missing Form 5472 package, include the statement, and ask the IRS to abate penalties when the facts support reasonable cause.
penalty.s033: How does the Form 5472 penalty rule work?
penalty.s034: The initial penalty applies per Form 5472, per year, and continuation penalties can add more after an IRS notice. We show both pieces together because the calculator is a statutory exposure estimate, not a prediction, and the ordinary next step is still to fix the filing with the missing package and reasonable-cause statement.
penalty.s036: The statute sets {value1} for each taxable year a reporting corporation fails to furnish the information, and the IRS applies it to each failure to file a complete and correct Form 5472. We count one Form 5472 per LLC per year, which assumes one related party (usually the foreign owner). The IRS manual asserts the initial penalty once per related party per taxable year, so an LLC that dealt with more related parties can face more.
penalty.s037: Continuation penalty: counted from your notice date
penalty.s038: If the failure continues more than {value1} days after the IRS mails notice of it, another {value2} applies for each {periodDays}-day period or part of one. The statute counts from the day the notice is mailed; we use the notice date you enter. Day {value3} starts the first period and each further {days1} days (or part) adds one, per LLC per year, up to today. The IRS says there is no maximum penalty amount.
penalty.s040: The IRS manual says the penalty may be assessed systemically during initial processing of a late Form 5472 attached to a late Form 1120, and that a CP 215 Notice of Penalty Charge is sent once a penalty is assessed. That is why the calculator treats the initial penalty as exposure from the day a return is late.
penalty.s042: Relief. The IRS can excuse a late Form 5472 for reasonable cause, case by case, and must apply that rule liberally to small corporations that meet its conditions. If reasonable cause existed, the {graceDays}-day period starts no earlier than the last day it did. First Time Abate isn't on the IRS's list of eligible penalties. The calculator shows none of these reductions.
penalty.s043: Filing late before the IRS contacts you
penalty.s044: If you're not under IRS examination or investigation and haven't been contacted about the missing returns, the IRS says to file them through normal filing procedures, and you may attach a reasonable-cause statement. Penalties may still be assessed.
penalty.s046: The time to assess tax for a return or period the Form 5472 information relates to doesn't expire until 3 years after the IRS is furnished that information, so that 3-year period hasn't started while the form is unfiled. If the failure was due to reasonable cause and not willful neglect, the rule covers only the related items.
penalty.s048: How does the calculator work out the estimate?
penalty.s049: The figures come from IRC §6038A(d) and the IRS's own guidance. Each rule below links to its primary source.
